newsitem.title: SOMALIA: 38 killed in renewed fighting in Mogadishu.
newsitem.headline: 38 killed in renewed fighting in Mogadishu.

text.p: At least 38 people were killed and more than 90 injured on Sunday when heavy fighting erupted in the Medina district of south Mogadishu between armed factions, witnesses reported.
The fighting between forces of warlord Hussein Mohamed Aideed and those of rival factions leaders Osman Hassan Ali Atto and Musa Sidi Yalahow followed a series of clashes last week in the same area.
Local residents said the fighting began late on Saturday night when Aideed's men entered the main market and began looting.
Market stalls, petrol stations were all looted, and several taxis were driven off by Aideed's men before the other armed groups arrived and drove them back.
The anti-Aideed group used heavily armed technicals -- makeshift armoured vehicles -- anti-aircraft missiles and mortars. Stray mortar rounds damaged houses in surrounding residential areas.
Among the civilian casualties was a family of nine, where only the father survived, residents said.
Sporadic gunfire continued after the main group of Aideed's men was driven back, and witnesses said both sides were trying to gain more territory.
A senior officer in the Aideed faction was quoted as telling his men this was only the beginning of the war.

Ali Mahdi Mohamed, whose forces control north Mogadishu, ordered the reinforcement of guards on the "green line" separating north and south Mogadishu, raising fears they might join the fighting if it erupted again.
